questions.topic: Errors in row reduction
questions.learningObjective: Spot an echelon form error
questions.stem: A teammate's row echelon form has a pivot to the right of a pivot above it; what is wrong?

answer.exemplar: In row echelon form each pivot must lie strictly to the right of the pivot in the row above; otherwise reduction is incomplete.

questions.explanation: Pivots must staircase to the right. A pivot left of or aligned with the one above violates echelon form.

questions.subject: INTEGRATED_3
questions.topic: No solution against infinitely many solutions
questions.learningObjective: Summarize solution types for planning systems
questions.stem: Explain how to determine whether a planning linear system has no, one, or infinitely many solutions.

answer.exemplar: Row reduce to RREF; a contradiction row means no solution, a pivot in every variable column means one solution, and a free variable means infinitely many.

questions.explanation: The reduced form exposes contradictions and free variables. Counting pivots versus variables decides uniqueness.
questions.hint: Check RREF for contradiction or free variables.
